span_sentences: Ukraine’s Computer Emergency Threat Response Team (CERT-UA) announced earlier this week that threat actors have been spotted using a Russian-made remote access trojan (RAT) against targets in the country.
CERT-UA spotted the campaign earlier this month.

“Typically, the mentioned archives contain a file with the extension ".pdf", as well as an executable file classified as DarkTortilla, which is a cryptor/loader type software tool, the purpose of which is to decrypt and launch (including by injection) the Dark Crystal RAT (DCRAT) remote control software tool,” reads the CERT-UA security advisory.
The perpetrators reportedly use rogue archived messages on Signal to spread malware.
The agency says the threat group, tracked as UAC-0200, has been targeting individuals in Ukraine’s Defense Forces and employees of defense-industrial organizations.
Threat actors launched a new malicious campaign against organizations in Ukraine’s defense sector, spreading Dark Crystal malware.
Dark Crystal (or DCRat) is a RAT allegedly favored by many novice hackers, but with an advanced enough design to fit the needs of more advanced attackers, as well.
